# Hard-to-vary report: “Oral infection by recPrP^Sc causes prion disease in wild-type mice”

## 1. The question, frozen
The title and opening fix the central question as **forward/production in mice**: does a single oral feeding of in-vitro-generated recPrP^Sc *produce* prion disease in wild-type C57BL/6 mice? Range: one recPrP^Sc batch, 50 µL, single feed, ~650-day watch. A second, wider claim rides on it — that this supports PrP^Sc as the agent of *orally transmitted natural* prion disease. That is a different question (a jump from mice to Kuru/BSE/CWD), so I keep it separate and mark it as the paper does.

## 2. The explanation in parts (owner’s words)
(a) recPrP^Sc made by sPMCA — aggregated, PK-resistant, “high titer.” (b) Single 50 µL oral feeding. (c) Mouse #9 sickened ~250 d, terminal ~40 d later. (d) PK-resistant PrP^Sc in #9 brain. (e) Histopathology: spongiosis, astrogliosis, microgliosis, PrP deposits. (f) Second-round i.c. transmission from #9 (191 dpi). (g) Controls: sPMCA substrate (negative), DBH (positive). (h) i.c. recPrP^Sc: 100% attack, 196 d. (i) Claim that the attack rate is “comparable to naturally occurring prions.” (j) Concluding claim: PrP^Sc is the cause of orally transmitted natural disease.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| (a) recPrP^Sc titer/content | **Held if** | Held only by the earlier titer paper (~10⁴ LD50/µg). This batch was **not titrated** — the paper says so. |
| (b) Single 50 µL oral feeding | **Fixed** | A copied protocol choice, not tested against mouth-pipette/dose alternatives. |
| (c) #9 sickened | **Held** | Removing the feeding (substrate controls) left mice well; so the feeding is what moves it. |
| (d) PK-resistant PrP^Sc in #9 | **Held** | Classic marker; absent in non-sick fed mice. |
| (e) Histopathology | **Two routes** | With (d), either alone shows PrP^Sc conversion; neither needs the other. Each may have a second job (d = biochemistry, e = pattern), so keep both only if so. |
| (f) Second-round transmission | **Held** | Load-bearing: it does the job of showing transmissibility, not a one-off. |
| (g) Substrate control | **Held** | Rules out pellet/procedure as cause — a real “did not happen” job. |
| (h) i.c. positive control | **Held** | Shows the inoculum is infectious and isolates route as the variable. |
| (i) “Comparable to natural prions” | **Borrowed + loose** | Rests on Sigurdson (6.4 LogLD50 → 1/11) and the prior titer paper; here untitrated, so a near neighbour (dose) could replace it. |
| (j) PrP^Sc causes natural oral disease | **Borrowed** | Rests on the prion hypothesis itself; the experiment tests mice, not sheep/cervids/humans. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

- **Flip.** Had #9 stayed well, the claim “oral recPrP^Sc is sufficient” would have failed — good, the claim risked something. But the *wider* claim (j) flips badly: if all 11 fed mice had stayed healthy, the paper could still say “dose too low, in vitro infectivity not shown orally.” A result that narrows rather than refutes is a patch; so (j) is easier to vary than the narrow claim.
- **Reverse.** The mice → disease direction is genuine (feeding produces disease), so (c)–(f) are the right direction for “what produces it.” Claim (j) runs backwards: it reads human/cervid outbreaks back into the mouse result.
- **Answer in the starting points.** (j) is close to the starting hypothesis. The experiment gives it independent support, so it is not purely circular — but (j) does not add reach beyond what the hypothesis already asserted.
- **Added job.** A clean test would be a **sham pellet** and a naïve mouse. These were not run; the substrate control partly covers the pellet, but not “an irrelevant protein.” The added job “the disease came from the fed material, not a spontaneous event” is *held only weakly* (1/11 vs 1/6 in DBH — the DBH group was actually sicker).
- **Pull.** (i) “comparable to natural prions” pulls against the same paper’s own “attack rate is low.” The line rests on a dose nobody measured; it could be wrong. Show a **naïve control** staying well and the line moves back to “low.”
- **Patches.** The paper is honest: low n, no titration, no dose escalation. No silent narrowing that I can see — “sufficient” is an existence claim, and one case can support existence.
- **Look inside.** “Survives digestion, maintains conformation, spreads to CNS” is stated, not shown. Outputs match; the workings are asserted. A change reaching inside (measure infectivity in gut/lymphoid tissue) is missing.
- **Watch the part.** “Clasping” appeared in mice #10, #14, #21 that had **no** disease. So clasping is a measurement that moves without the thing; only (d)+(f) hold the disease in place. Do not let clasping carry a case alone.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary
1. **Titrate the fed batch and add the missing controls** (naïve mouse; sham pellet; vehicle-fed group). That would hold (a) and shrink the rival.
2. **A second oral round- passage** — the paper proposes this — would turn (f) from a mouse-only result into an oral-transmission claim, tightening (j).

## 6. What this does not show
Hard to vary is not true. Part (j) passing or failing here neither proves nor disproves the prion hypothesis. Absence of a spontaneous case in untreated mice is *unknown*, not evidence against (j).

## 7. One next step
Run the **naïve + sham-pellet controls** and **titrate the batch to bite**. That is the change that would most tighten the one part — (a)/(i) — that currently only rests on earlier work, and leave (j) either held or plainly loose.

- Best rival: "The disease in #9 was a spontaneous/age-related prion event or a cage contamination." What change separates? Substrate-fed mice stayed healthy, and #9 alone among 11 got sick. - Pull: "low attack rate" vs "dose comparable to natural prions" — the paper says attack rate is LOW but also claims it's COMPARABLE to natural prions. These pull. Which gives? The title/statement "is sufficient to cause prion disease" — one case suffices to show sufficiency (existence claim). Good.

- Look inside: The mechanism (survives digestion, spreads to CNS) is asserted, not traced. The paper says "indicate that... is able to survive the digestion, maintain conformation, spread to CNS."
